payload.claim: `stacking_kwarg = {"parent" + "_branch": target_branch}` builds the `package()` keyword by string concatenation specifically so the literal token `parent_branch` never appears in `saffron/cli.py`, which is exactly what keeps `tests/test_package.py::test_the_operators_reachable_packaging_path_is_unstacked` (`assert "parent_branch" not in Path(cli.__file__).read_text()`) green. That test's own docstring says its purpose is to prove 'the one caller reaching `package()` in production must not pass a parent' — a claim this diff makes false in behavior while keeping it true in spelling. The guard now passes for a reason unrelated to what it was written to detect, so a later refactor that inlines the concatenation (or a rename that makes it read naturally) would silently re-trip a check whose premise this spec already defeated, and nothing but a text search would show that the safety net it names is gone.
